title: Property Stolen and Recovered
pdf_title: CHAPTER-12 PROPERTY STOLEN AND RECOVERED Value of Property Stolen & Recovered - National Level 12.1.1 The details of the property stolen and subsequently recovered alongwith the percentage of recovery (year-wise) during the decade 1986-96 have been presented in Table-73. The percentage changes in these attributes over the decade have also been shown in this table. 12.1.2 During the year 1996, property worth Rs. 99,670 lakhs was reported stolen in the country. This loss was lower by 6.2 per cent over the previous year. However, the value of property lost increased by 354.6 per cent during the decade 1986-96. 12.1.3 Property worth Rs. 28,142 lakhs was recovered during 1996 as against property lost (stolen) of Rs. 99,670 lakhs. The value of property recovered showed an addition of 9.4 per cent over the previous year. Such recoveries in terms of percentage, recorded an increase of 269.6 per cent over the value of the property recovered in 1986. 12.1.4 The share of recovery during the year increased to 28.2 per cent as against 24.2 per cent in the previous year. The recovery percentage during the decade was, however, observed to be the highest at 34.7 in 1986 and lowest at 15.6 per cent in 1993. Value of Property Stolen & Recovered - States, UTs and Metropolitan Cities 12.2.1 The State, UT and City-wise details regarding the value of property stolen and recovered as also the percentage of recovery during 1996 can be seen in Table-74. Maharashtra's share towards the property stolen was the highest at Rs. 27,657.6 lakhs followed by Uttar Pradesh (Rs. 9776.1 lakhs), Delhi (Rs. 9,456.2 lakhs), Gujarat (9,314.1 lakhs) and Karnataka (5,708.5 lakhs). Maharashtra was also able to achieve maximum recoveries of the property worth Rs. 4,522.1 lakhs during 1996. However, the highest (59.1%) recovery percentage was to be in Haryana and the lowest in Manipur (4.9%). Amongst the 23 mega Cities, Bombay recorded a significantly high loss of property worth Rs. 18,236.3 lakhs, sharing 65.9 per cent of its domain State, Maharashtra.
